segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the rollout details for the support analytics package before we send the order form over.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re still at 42 seats for the first phase, right? That’s 36 agents, four team leads, and two admins.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, 42 seats total. The annual subscription comes to $31,080, and implementation is the one-time $4,500 services line.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And invoicing, can you do net 30 with the invoice dated March 1? Our finance team wants it in the March close.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, net 30 is standard for us. We can set the subscription start date to March 1 and invoice on that date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. For go-live, we’re targeting April 15. Is that still realistic if we sign by next Friday?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If the signed order is back by February 23, we’ll schedule kickoff the week of March 4. That leaves about six weeks for setup, training, and the data validation session.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. One thing on the term, procurement asked if this can be a 12-month agreement with no auto-renewal, just renewal by written notice.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can do 12 months and remove auto-renewal. I’ll have that reflected in the terms section.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send it to me and copy Marcus in procurement. If it matches what we discussed, I can route it today.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the order form and the services summary this afternoon, and I’ll include the March 1 start date, 42 seats, net 30, and April 15 go-live target.
